title: Rule-based access to learning materials in a Flipped class in embedded programming
reason: Per-student LMS access counts (in-class slides, pre-class slides, quizzes) correlated (Spearman) with rated assignment documentation and program quality, and with hand-in completion, in two spring cohorts. Meets I1; no p-values, subsample sizes unclear.

extraction.design: correlational practice paper, two cohorts (with/without rule-based access), Spearman
extraction.population: 2nd-semester Bachelor of Engineering (electro technology) students, embedded programming course, 1 university
extraction.lms_indicators: LMS clicks on in-class slides, pre-class slides, pre-class quiz participation
extraction.outcome_or_construct: assignment documentation quality (0–2) and program quality (-1/0/1); assignment hand-in

effect_sizes.between: in-class slide access ↔ documentation quality, assignment 2, spring 2023
effect_sizes.location: Table 2 (columns doc_sl, doc_psl, doc_q, pro_sl, pro_psl)

effect_sizes.between: in-class slide access ↔ documentation quality, assignment 2, spring 2024
in-class slide access ↔ documentation quality, assignment 3, spring 2023
in-class slide access ↔ documentation quality, assignment 3, spring 2024
all students' in-class slide access ↔ hand-in of program and journal, assignment 2, spring 2024
effect_sizes.quote: program and journal (for assignment 2) in correlation to the slides used in class it ... shows correlation by 0.40 and for assignment 3 hand-in correlated to in class slides

extraction.notes: Enrolment 48 (spring 2023) and 68 (spring 2024), but Table 2 uses only students in groups with incomplete assignments; that subsample n is not given. No p-values or CIs. Text's '0.33 ... for assignment 3' does not match Table 2 (0,015). Further: assignment 3 hand-in rho 0.28 (2024), 0.35 (2023), assignment 2 0.060 (2023).
